facts.title: Casa Latina (Center for Hispanic Excellence)
facts.summary: Casa Latina promotes awareness of Latinx issues, culture, and identity at Penn through programs, events, and dialogues on issues affecting Latinx communities locally, nationally, and internationally.
facts.hook: hosts programs and dialogues on issues affecting Latinx communities locally and nationally
facts.quote: Casa Latina promotes greater awareness of Latinx issues, culture, and identity at the University of Pennsylvania. Casa Latina works closely with the Penn community to offer a supportive environment where all students are welcomed and engaged in programs, events, and dialogues that address important issues affecting Latinxs locally, nationally, and internationally.
facts.sourceTitle: Center for Hispanic Excellence: Casa Latina Latina - Casa Latina

facts.title: Center for Undergraduate Research and Fellowships (CURF)
facts.nameOnPage: Center for Undergraduate Research and Fellowships
facts.summary: CURF supports Penn students pursuing undergraduate research, scholars programs, and fellowships, and promotes connections and mentorship between faculty and students.
facts.hook: helps students find faculty mentors, research opportunities, and fellowships
facts.quote: The Center for Undergraduate Research and Fellowships (CURF) supports all students as they pursue transformative experiences through fellowships, scholars programs, and undergraduate research. CURF promotes connections between faculty and students, encourages mentorship, and educates the Penn community about opportunities for all students and alumni.
facts.sourceTitle: About Us | Penn CURF

facts.title: Kelly Writers House
facts.summary: Founded in 1995, the Kelly Writers House is a 13-room house on Locust Walk that serves writers from Penn and the Philadelphia region and hosts about 150 public programs each semester.
facts.hook: offers a 13-room house on Locust Walk that hosts about 150 public programs each semester
facts.quote: Founded in 1995 by a group of students, faculty, staff and alumni, the Kelly Writers House is an actual 13-room house at 3805 Locust Walk on Penn's campus that serves as a center for writers of all kinds from Penn and the Philadelphia region at large. Each semester the Writers House hosts approximately 150 public programs and projects
facts.sourceTitle: About the Kelly Writers House
facts.commonnessReason: One of the most frequently cited Penn landmarks in applicant essays.

facts.title: Netter Center for Community Partnerships
facts.summary: Founded in 1992, the Netter Center builds place-based partnerships between Penn and West Philadelphia on problems such as health inequities, environmental sustainability, and unequal education.
facts.hook: connects students to place-based research, teaching, and service partnerships in West Philadelphia
facts.quote: Founded in 1992, the Barbara and Edward Netter Center for Community Partnerships ... help solve universal problems such as poverty, health inequities, environmental sustainability, and inadequate, unequal education ... The Netter Center develops and helps implement democratic, mutually transformative, place-based partnerships between Penn and West Philadelphia that advance research, teaching, learning, and service.
facts.sourceTitle: About the Center | Netter Center for Community Partnerships
facts.commonnessReason: Penn's best-known community engagement center, frequently named in Penn essays.

facts.title: Penn First Plus
facts.summary: Penn First Plus is Penn's hub for first-generation students, including the four-week Pre-First Year Program that precedes New Student Orientation.
facts.hook: supports first-generation students, including a four-week summer program before orientation
facts.quote: Penn is a place for firsts, and Penn First Plus serves as Penn’s hub for making the Penn undergraduate experience more welcoming ... for first generation students ... Part of Penn First Plus, the Pre-First Year Program (PFP) is an intensive four-week summer program preceding New Student Orientation (NSO)
facts.sourceTitle: Penn First Plus | Penn Admissions

facts.title: The Water Center at Penn
facts.summary: The Water Center at Penn is a center for urban water policy, innovation, and science that engages faculty and students and takes an integrated approach to water supply, stormwater, and water quality.
facts.hook: connects students to urban water policy work on water supply, stormwater systems, and water quality
facts.quote: The Water Center at Penn is a center for urban water policy, innovation, and science that engages University faculty and students ... integrating planning for water supply, wastewater and stormwater systems, protecting human health, and improving water quality.
facts.sourceTitle: The Water Center | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: Venture Lab
facts.summary: Venture Lab, a partnership of Wharton, Penn Engineering, and the Weitzman School of Design, is a starting point for any Penn student or alum interested in entrepreneurship and innovation.
facts.hook: gives students from every Penn school a starting point for entrepreneurship and innovation
facts.quote: Venture Lab is a partnership by The Wharton School, Penn Engineering, and The Stuart Weitzman School of Design that provides a physical start here button to serve all students and alumni across the University of Pennsylvania who are interested in entrepreneurship and innovation.
facts.sourceTitle: Homepage

facts.title: EAS 2020: Rivers in a Changing World
facts.nameOnPage: EAS 2020: Rivers in a Changing World
facts.summary: An ABCS course built on a partnership with Sayre High School that uses an environmental river laboratory steps from Cobbs Creek for hands-on learning by Sayre students alongside Penn undergraduates.
facts.hook: has Penn undergraduates learn alongside Sayre High School students at a river laboratory beside Cobbs Creek
facts.quote: to develop an Academically Based Community Service (ABCS) course on “Rivers in a changing world”. ... The unique setting of an environmental river laboratory that is just steps from a natural river (Cobbs Creek), and close to Sayre High School, presents a special opportunity for meaningful hands-on learning of Sayre students in collaboration with Penn undergraduates.
facts.sourceTitle: Fall 2026 ABCS Courses | Netter Center for Community Partnerships

facts.title: EAS 3990: Pre-College Robotics Education
facts.summary: In this ABCS engineering course, students learn robotics basics including rapid prototyping and Arduino programming, then mentor classroom robotics projects in a Philadelphia public school.
facts.hook: teaches Arduino programming and prototyping, then has students mentor robotics in a Philadelphia public school
facts.quote: This Academically-Based Community Service (ABCS) course combines community engagement with education research to prepare Penn students to conduct impactful engineering teaching and outreach. Students will learn robotics basics (multi-body kinematics, rapid prototyping, and arduino programming) and then help mentor classroom robotics projects in a Philadelphia public school.
facts.sourceTitle: Fall 2026 ABCS Courses | Netter Center for Community Partnerships

facts.title: EESC 4300: Meteorology and Atmospheric Science
facts.summary: An atmospheric science course on the physical processes that shape weather and climate, tied to hurricanes, heat waves, and urban heat islands at scales from neighborhood microclimates to the whole planet.
facts.hook: explains urban heat islands and neighborhood microclimates through atmospheric physics
facts.quote: From hurricanes and heat waves to climate change and urban heat islands, atmospheric science sits at the center of some of today's most urgent environmental challenges. ... Students explore the structure and composition of the atmosphere and the physical processes that shape weather and climate ... from neighborhood urban microclimates to the entire planet
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: EESC 4630: Hydrology
facts.summary: An introduction to the hydrologic cycle and water budgets, stream flow, flood hydrograph analysis, groundwater flow, well hydraulics, and water quality.
facts.hook: covers stream flow, flood hydrographs, groundwater flow, and water quality fundamentals
facts.quote: Introduction to the basic principles of the hydrologic cycle and water budgets, precipitation and infiltration, evaporation and transpiration, stream flow, hydrograph analysis (floods), subsurface and groundwater flow, well hydraulics, water quality, and frequency analysis.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Fall 2026 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: EESC 4700: Remote Sensing
facts.summary: A remote sensing course that teaches Google Earth Engine analysis, including thermal imagery, as student teams partner with community organizations on environmental questions.
facts.hook: has student teams use remote sensing and thermal imagery to answer community partners' environmental questions
facts.quote: analysis of remotely sensed data using Google Earth Engine will be emphasized. ... multispectral, hyperspectral, and thermal imagery; image interpretation; and spatial analysis. ... Working in teams, students partner with community organizations, schools, agencies, or other stakeholders to identify an environmental question, challenge, or information need that can be addressed using remote sensing.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Fall 2026 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: ENVS 1615: Urban Environments: Speaking About Lead in West Philadelphia
facts.summary: In this ABCS course, students study the epidemiology and exposure pathways of lead poisoning, then work with West Philadelphia teachers to apply lead research with middle school students.
facts.hook: has students teach West Philadelphia middle schoolers to apply lead-exposure research to their own neighborhoods
facts.quote: In ENVS 1615, Penn undergraduates learn about the epidemiology of lead poisoning, the pathways of exposure, and methods for community outreach and education. Penn students collaborate with middle school and high school teachers in West Philadelphia to engage middle school children in exercises that apply environmental research relating to lead poisoning to their homes and neighborhoods.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Fall 2026 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: ENVS 2390: Freshwater Ecology
facts.summary: A survey of the physical, chemical, and biological properties of freshwater ecosystems, both flowing and still, natural and polluted.
facts.hook: surveys the physics, chemistry, and biology of natural and polluted freshwater ecosystems
facts.quote: Survey of the physical, chemical and biological properties of freshwater ecosystems, both riverine and lentic, natural and polluted.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: ENVS 3053 / SPAN 3910: Sustainable Development and Culture in Latin America
facts.summary: An upper-level seminar for Spanish majors and minors that examines the environmental, economic, and social dimensions of sustainable development through peyote, coca, and coffee in Latin America.
facts.hook: studies sustainable development in Latin America in an upper-level seminar for Spanish students
facts.quote: This interdisciplinary course exposes students to the three dimensions of sustainable development -environmental, economic, and social- through an examination of three products -peyote, coca, and coffee- that are crucial in shaping modern identity in areas of Latin America. ... This is an upper level seminar open to majors and minors of Spanish
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: ENVS 3100: Environmental Case Studies
facts.summary: This course analyzes one or two environmental case studies each week through debates, action plans, role-playing, and group decision-making simulations.
facts.hook: uses weekly debates, role-play, and decision simulations to analyze environmental cases
facts.quote: The class analyzes 1-2 case studies each week, beginning with at-home preparatory assignments for each class, followed by in-class activities such as debates, drafting action plans, role-playing and group decision-making simulations.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: ENVS 3700: GIS Mapping Places and Analyzing Spaces
facts.summary: A hands-on introduction to geographic information systems that builds the skills for basic GIS projects and advanced GIS coursework, with no prior GIS experience required.
facts.hook: teaches the GIS skills needed to map and analyze spatial data for projects and advanced coursework
facts.quote: This course is a hands-on introduction to the concepts and capabilities of geographic information systems (GIS). Students will develop the skills necessary for carrying out basic GIS projects and for advanced GIS coursework. ... Previous experience in the use of GIS is not required.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: ENVS 4250: Our Water Planet
facts.summary: A course that uses case studies to examine water issues in the Anthropocene and the outlook for water quality and availability in an era of rapid environmental change, with a local field trip.
facts.hook: examines the future of water quality and availability through case studies and a local field trip
facts.quote: use topical case studies to examine water issues in the Anthropocene and examine what lies in store for water quality and availability in the twenty-first century during an era of rapid environmental change. ... This course will include a local field trip.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: ENVS 4330: Climate and Environmental Communication: Theory and Application
facts.summary: A course on how climate science reaches the public through forms such as consensus statements, op-eds, court briefs, fact checks, and speeches.
facts.hook: analyzes how climate science is communicated through op-eds, court briefs, fact checks, and speeches
facts.quote: This course will focus on understanding the multiple ways in which climate science is communicated to publics and how they come to understand it. ... Forms of communication on which the class will focus include consensus statements, manifestos, commentaries, court briefs, news accounts, fact checks, op-eds, letters to the editor, speeches, and media interviews.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Earth and Environmental Sciences
facts.commonnessReason: Co-taught by Michael Mann, a widely known climate scientist whom applicants may already mention.

facts.title: JWST 1120: Translating Cultures: Literature on and in Translation
facts.summary: A course that reads autobiography, fiction, poetry, and literary theory to ask what it means to translate and to live between two languages.
facts.hook: explores what it means to translate and to live between two languages
facts.quote: With a diverse group of readings--autobiography, fiction, poetry, anthology, and literary theory--this course will address some fundamental questions about translating language and culture. What does it mean to translate? How do we read a text in translation? What does it mean to live between two languages? Who is a translator?
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Penn Language Center

facts.title: SPAN 1005: Advanced Spanish for Medical Professions
facts.summary: An advanced Spanish course for students headed toward health careers that builds medical vocabulary through contemporary health topics and covers health care issues affecting Hispanic/Latino patients.
facts.hook: builds advanced medical Spanish and awareness of health care issues facing Hispanic/Latino patients
facts.quote: The goal of this course is to provide advanced practice in Spanish to those students who are interested in pursuing careers in the medical and health care fields. ... Students will also gain awareness of those health care issues affecting the Hispanic/Latino patient.
facts.sourceTitle: Courses for Spring 2027 | Penn Language Center

facts.title: STAT 4929: Community Data Science
facts.summary: An ABCS statistics course in which student teams solve data science problems for community organizations, with possible projects including heat islands in West Philadelphia.
facts.hook: puts data science skills to work for community groups on projects such as West Philadelphia heat islands
facts.quote: This course provides students with the opportunity to hone their data science skills and gain practical experience by working with a community organization on a data science problem of interest to the organization. ... Heat islands in West Philadelphia ... This is an Academically Based Community Service (ABCS) course.
facts.sourceTitle: Fall 2026 ABCS Courses | Netter Center for Community Partnerships

facts.title: Engineering Studios @ Venture Lab
facts.summary: The Engineering Studios at Venture Lab are fabrication labs open to the whole Penn community, with free 3D printing and laser cutting and a mechatronics lab for electrical projects.
facts.hook: provides free 3D printing, laser cutting, and a mechatronics lab for student building projects
facts.quote: The Engineering Studios @ Venture Lab are a collection of fabrication labs open to the entire University of Pennsylvania community ... The Prototyping studio offers basic hand tools, and 3D printing and laser cutting services free of charge. ... Access to Mechatronics Lab for your electrical projects.
facts.sourceTitle: Engineering Studios
facts.commonnessReason: A makerspace of the kind most engineering schools offer.

facts.title: Penn Farm at Penn Park
facts.summary: The Penn Farm, which grew out of the Penn Food and Wellness Collaborative, engages the Penn community around wellness, food access, sustainability, and education.
facts.hook: involves students in a campus farm focused on food access, wellness, and sustainability
facts.quote: The Penn Farm, which originated through the Penn Food and Wellness Collaborative (PFWC), is a unique, multidisciplinary initiative that engages stakeholders from across the Penn community around four central pillars of wellness, food access, sustainability, and education.
facts.sourceTitle: Penn Farm | Penn Sustainability

facts.title: Howard Neukrug, Professor of Practice in Earth and Environmental Science
facts.summary: Howard Neukrug, a Professor of Practice in Earth and Environmental Science, is the former Commissioner and CEO of Philadelphia Water, whose water system serves 2.3 million people.
facts.hook: brings experience leading Philadelphia Water's drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater system
facts.quote: Mr. Neukrug is the former Commissioner and CEO of Philadelphia Water ... for its drinking water/wastewater/stormwater system serving 2.3 million people. He is currently a Professor of Practice in the Earth and Environmental Sciences Department
facts.sourceTitle: Howard Neukrug | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: Hugo N. Ulloa, Assistant Professor of Earth and Environmental Science
facts.summary: Hugo Ulloa studies the physics of transport and mixing in natural waters such as lakes and coastal seas, blending theory, numerical modeling, and laboratory and field observations.
facts.hook: studies how water moves and mixes in lakes and coastal seas using models plus lab and field observations
facts.quote: My research focuses on characterizing the physics governing transport and mixing processes in natural waters, such as lakes and coastal seas. For this, I blend theory, high-resolution numerical modelling with laboratory and field observations.
facts.sourceTitle: Hugo N. Ulloa | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: Jon Hawkings, Assistant Professor of Earth and Environmental Science
facts.summary: Jon Hawkings studies how glacial meltwater shapes downstream biogeochemical cycles, relying heavily on field sampling and electrochemical sensor deployment.
facts.hook: researches meltwater chemistry through field sampling and deployed electrochemical sensors
facts.quote: My current research focuses on the role of glacial meltwater in downstream biogeochemical cycles. ... A large part of my research is based on field observations (sample collection for analysis in labs and electrochemical sensor deployment).
facts.sourceTitle: Jon Hawkings | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: Oceans & Climate Group @Penn
facts.summary: The Oceans & Climate Group runs global climate models and studies their output; its Digital Climate Atlas is an online visualization of over 200 geospatial datasets, including IPCC projections of warming impacts.
facts.hook: runs global climate models and offers an online climate atlas of more than 200 geospatial datasets
facts.quote: We run global climate models and study their output ... The Digital Climate Atlas is an online climate visualization project. It includes over 200 geospatial datasets and includes IPCC projections for how temperature increases will impact places around the world.
facts.sourceTitle: Oceans and Climate |

facts.title: Penn ATmospheric Multiscale Observations & Simulations (ATMOS) Lab
facts.summary: The ATMOS Lab studies how surface turbulence interacts with the atmosphere from microclimates to regional climate, with a research area on heat, mass, and momentum transfer in cities.
facts.hook: investigates urban microclimates and how heat moves through cities
facts.quote: The ATMOS Lab studies how turbulent processes at the Earth’s surface interact with the atmosphere across scales, from microclimates to regional weather and climate. ... Urban Microclimate & Atmospheric Physics ... Fundamental understanding of heat, mass, and momentum transfer in cities.
facts.sourceTitle: Atmos-Lab – Penn Arts & Sciences

facts.title: Penn GEFLOW Lab
facts.summary: The Penn GEFLOW Lab studies fluid physics in nature, including a project on how extreme rainfall becomes urban flood waves, and lists senior thesis research among its openings for undergraduates.
facts.hook: offers undergraduates senior thesis research on natural flows such as urban flooding from extreme rainfall
facts.quote: This project aims to develop an interdisciplinary framework to predict how extreme rainfall events become flood waves in urban environments and quantify its impacts. ... Undergraduate student – Senior thesis
facts.sourceTitle: Penn GEFLOW Lab – Exploring the Physics of Fluids in Nature

facts.title: Plante Lab at Penn
facts.summary: The Plante Lab studies what stabilizes and destabilizes organic matter in mineral soils and mentors undergraduate students in its research program.
facts.hook: mentors undergraduates in soil science research on how organic matter persists in soils
facts.quote: We seek to characterize and understand the mechanisms that stabilize and destabilize organic matter in mineral soils. ... Mentoring postdocs, graduate and undergraduate students in our research program, teaching graduate and undergraduate courses using active learning techniques, and K12 teaching and outreach on the importance of soils.
facts.sourceTitle: Plante Lab @ Penn | Soil Science and Terrestrial Biogeochemistry Research at Penn

facts.title: Price Lab for Digital Humanities
facts.summary: The Price Lab for Digital Humanities helps humanities scholars become creators and critics of technology through cross-disciplinary collaboration and digital skill-sharing at all levels.
facts.hook: builds digital and computational skills for humanities students through cross-disciplinary collaboration
facts.quote: Welcome to the Price Lab for Digital Humanities at the University of Pennsylvania. Our mission is to empower humanities scholars to become more confident creators and critics of technology. Toward that end, we provide a space for exploratory collaborations across the disciplines, as well as digital skill-sharing at all levels of experience and expertise.
facts.sourceTitle: What We Do | Price Lab for Digital Humanities

facts.title: Academically Based Community Service (ABCS) courses with West Philadelphia partners
facts.summary: In Academically Based Community Service courses, Penn students and faculty work with West Philadelphia public schools, communities of faith, and community organizations on shared problems.
facts.hook: takes coursework into West Philadelphia public schools, congregations, and community organizations
facts.quote: Academically Based Community Service is at the core of the Netter Center’s work. ABCS students and faculty work with West Philadelphia public schools, communities of faith, and community organizations to help solve critical campus and community problems.
facts.sourceTitle: Off-campus Learning | University of Pennsylvania
facts.commonnessReason: ABCS is a signature Penn model that some applicants mention, though specific ABCS courses are rarely named.

facts.title: Civic Sustainability Fellowship with Philadelphia city agencies
facts.summary: A paid eleven-week summer fellowship placing Penn students with city agencies and nonprofits on sustainability; hosts have included the Office of Sustainability and Philadelphia Energy Authority.
facts.hook: places students in paid summer roles that support Philadelphia's sustainability goals
facts.quote: This eleven-week paid summer program places research interns in summer positions with city agencies and non-profit organization to support the City’s sustainability objectives and provide professional development and real-world learning opportunities to Penn students. ... Organizations have included: ... City of Philadelphia’s Office of Sustainability ... Philadelphia Energy Authority
facts.sourceTitle: Civic Sustainability Fellowship | Penn Sustainability

facts.title: Morris Arboretum & Gardens
facts.summary: Penn's Morris Arboretum & Gardens is a historic public garden and educational institution that hosts year-round programming integrating art, science, and environmental stewardship.
facts.hook: offers year-round programming that combines art, science, and environmental stewardship
facts.quote: A historic public garden and educational institution, the Morris Arboretum & Gardens hosts year-round programming that integrates art, science, and environmental stewardship.
facts.sourceTitle: Arts & Culture | University of Pennsylvania

facts.title: Quaker Consortium courses at Bryn Mawr, Haverford, and Swarthmore
facts.summary: Through the Quaker Consortium, Penn students can study at Bryn Mawr, Haverford, or Swarthmore Colleges during the fall and spring terms.
facts.hook: lets students take fall and spring courses at Bryn Mawr, Haverford, or Swarthmore
facts.quote: Penn students have a unique opportunity to study at Bryn Mawr, Haverford, or Swarthmore Colleges during the fall and spring terms of the academic year.
facts.sourceTitle: Off-campus Learning | University of Pennsylvania

facts.title: Artificial Intelligence, BSE
facts.summary: Penn Engineering offers an in-person BSE in Artificial Intelligence, described as the first Ivy League AI engineering degree, that integrates computer science, robotics, ethics, and data science.
facts.hook: combines computer science, robotics, ethics, and data science in an undergraduate AI engineering degree
facts.quote: Penn Engineering; Offered In-Person; First Ivy League BSE in AI integrating CS, robotics, ethics, and data science.
facts.sourceTitle: Education | Penn AI
facts.commonnessReason: Widely publicized as the first Ivy League undergraduate AI degree, so many applicants cite it.

facts.title: Computational Neuroscience Minor
facts.summary: Penn's cross-school Computational Neuroscience minor gives students who study the brain quantitative skills and teaches neuroscience to students already trained in quantitative methods.
facts.hook: pairs quantitative training with neuroscience for students coming from either side
facts.quote: The Neuroscience Program has established a cross-school, inter-disciplinary Minor in Computational Neuroscience ... The minor provides quantitative skills to those already studying the brain, and teaches neuroscience to those already immersed in quantitative methodologies.
facts.sourceTitle: Computational Neuroscience Minor | Neuroscience

facts.title: Environmental Studies Major
facts.summary: Penn's Environmental Studies major aims to graduate students who can model environmental systems, collect and manage complex data sets, and work with environmental data in software.
facts.hook: trains students to model environmental systems and to collect and manage complex data sets
facts.quote: Graduates can also develop basic models of geographic, environmental or geologic systems. Graduates can collect and manage a complex data set. They can also manipulate environmental data with computer software.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Studies | Earth and Environmental Sciences
facts.commonnessReason: The intended major itself is often named by applicants, but its data and modeling objectives are rarely cited.

facts.title: Environmental Studies: Environmental Policy & Application concentration
facts.summary: An Environmental Studies concentration on the social and management aspects of environmental problems, in which community-based ABCS courses are strongly recommended.
facts.hook: pairs environmental policy coursework with strongly recommended community-based ABCS courses
facts.quote: Students in the Environmental Policy and Application acquire a background in the social and management aspects of environmental problems. ABCS courses in ENVS are strongly recommended for this concentration.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Studies | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: Impact, Value, and Sustainable Business (IVSB) concentration
facts.summary: Starting in 2026-27, Wharton undergraduates can concentrate in Impact, Value, and Sustainable Business, with an optional Business, Energy, Environment and Sustainability (BEES) specialization.
facts.hook: lets Wharton students specialize in business, energy, environment, and sustainability
facts.quote: Starting in the 2026-2027 academic year, Wharton undergraduate students can declare a concentration in Impact, Value, and Sustainable Business (IVSB). ... IVSB concentrators may choose to earn one of two transcript-level specializations—Business, Energy, Environment and Sustainability (BEES) or Social and Governance (SOGO)
facts.sourceTitle: Undergraduate Concentration: Impact, Value, and Sustainable Business - Impact, Value, and Sustainable Business Initiative

facts.title: Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) major
facts.summary: PPE is an interdisciplinary major in which students design a thematic concentration of challenging classes, with themes such as Public Policy and Governance and Distributive Justice.
facts.hook: lets students build a cross-disciplinary concentration in themes like public policy and governance
facts.quote: PPE is an interdisciplinary major that aims teach its majors how to think and work interdisciplinarily. ... Students design a thematic concentration composed of challenging classes, allowing them to think deeply about interdisciplinary topics ... Public Policy and Governance ... Distributive Justice
facts.sourceTitle: Thematic Concentrations | Philosophy Politics & Economics

facts.title: Community School Student Partnerships (CSSP)
facts.summary: CSSP is an undergraduate organization that works with Netter Center community schools to run school-day and after-school programs for children and families at four West Philadelphia schools.
facts.hook: lets students help run school-day and after-school programs at four West Philadelphia schools
facts.quote: Community School Student Partnerships (CSSP) is an undergraduate student organization that works in close collaboration with the Netter Center’s university-assisted community schools to provide academic and cultural enrichment to children and families in West Philadelphia. Penn students help operate school day and after school programs in four local schools.
facts.sourceTitle: Community School Student Partnerships | Netter Center for Community Partnerships

facts.title: Penn Band
facts.summary: The student-run Penn Band, part of Penn's Department of Athletics, performs upwards of 100 times during the academic year.
facts.hook: performs more than 100 times a year as a student-run band within Penn Athletics
facts.quote: The Penn Band—guardians of all things “Red and Blue”—is a part of the Department of Athletics at Penn. It stands among the largest and most active student-run organizations on-campus, performing upwards of 100 times during the academic year.
facts.sourceTitle: Performing Arts | Penn Admissions

facts.title: Penn Cycling & Triathlon sport club
facts.summary: Cycling & Triathlon appears in Penn Campus Recreation's sport club directory; sport clubs operate under the Sport Club Council and the Campus Recreation Department.
facts.hook: lets riders join a cycling and triathlon sport club under Penn Campus Recreation
facts.quote: Sport Clubs fall under the direction of the Sport Club Council (SCC) and the Campus Recreation Department. ... Cycling & Triathlon
facts.sourceTitle: Sport Club Directory - Penn Campus Recreation

facts.title: Penn Debate Society
facts.summary: Founded in 1984, the Penn Debate Society is Penn's competitive parliamentary debate team in the American Parliamentary Debate Association, with members from engineering to English.
facts.hook: competes in parliamentary debate in the American Parliamentary Debate Association
facts.quote: The Penn Debate Society (PDS) was founded in 1984 as the Penn Parliamentary Debate Society as part of the Penn Debate Council. Today, we are Penn's nationally ranked competitive debate team in the American Parliamentary Debate Association ... Our debaters range from engineering students to English majors and hail from all around the world.
facts.sourceTitle: Social Fundraising
facts.commonnessReason: Most universities have a debate team; useful for the swap test.

facts.title: Penn Environmental Group and other undergraduate sustainability groups
facts.summary: Penn's undergraduate environmental and climate student groups include the Penn Environmental Group, Penn Climate Ventures, the Penn Beekeeping Club, and the Penn Outdoors Club.
facts.hook: offers student-run environmental, climate, beekeeping, and outdoors clubs
facts.quote: Penn is home to numerous undergraduate student groups focused on environmental interests, climate action, and sustainability. Penn Outdoors Club, Penn Beekeeping Club, Penn Climate Ventures, and Penn Environmental Group are just a few.
facts.sourceTitle: Sustainability Student Groups | Penn Sustainability
facts.commonnessReason: Most universities have an environmental club; useful mainly for the swap test.

facts.title: Penn for Immigrant Rights (PIR)
facts.summary: Penn for Immigrant Rights is a student advocacy group that educates the Penn campus and the Philadelphia community about immigration through demonstrations and workshops.
facts.hook: runs workshops for Penn and Philadelphia audiences that address misconceptions about immigration
facts.quote: Penn for Immigrant Rights (PIR) is a social and political advocacy group dedicated to opening up the dialogue about undocumented immigrants and immigration in general. We strive to educate Penn’s campus and the Philadelphia community through demonstrations and workshops that seek to dismantle misconceptions about immigration
facts.sourceTitle: Latinx Student Groups - Casa Latina

facts.title: Penn Geology Society
facts.summary: The Penn Geology Society, formed in 2016, organizes local and regional field trips to geologically significant sites and welcomes any student interested in geology or environmental science.
facts.hook: runs local and regional geology field trips open to students interested in earth or environmental science
facts.quote: The Penn Geology Society formed in 2016 with the goal of fostering an environment where students with a passion for Earth science can come together to learn, grow, and develop. ... Organize field trips to geologically significant sites at both the local and regional level. ... all students with an interest in geology, environmental science, or related fields are welcome to join.
facts.sourceTitle: Penn Geology Society | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: Penn Jazz Ensembles
facts.summary: The Music Department's Penn Jazz Ensembles are directed by Philadelphia-area professionals and open to all students by audition; undergraduates can earn credit through MUSC 0070.
facts.hook: lets students audition into professionally led jazz ensembles and earn MUSC 0070 credit
facts.quote: These ensembles, directed by leading professionals in the Philadelphia area, are open to all students, faculty, staff, and community members by audition ... Penn Jazz Ensembles ... Undergraduate students may elect to receive credit (0.5 credit/semester as MUSC 0070) for their participation in these professionally-led Department ensembles.
facts.sourceTitle: Ensembles | Department of Music
facts.commonnessReason: Most universities offer jazz ensembles; useful for the swap test.

facts.title: Performing Arts Council at Platt Student Performing Arts House
facts.summary: Platt Student Performing Arts House is home to the Performing Arts Council, an umbrella for 46 student-run comedy, spoken word, dance, theater, and music groups.
facts.hook: connects students to 46 student-run comedy, spoken word, dance, theater, and music groups
facts.quote: Platt House is home to The Performing Arts Council, an umbrella organization for 46 student-run comedy, spoken word, dance, theater, and music organizations.
facts.sourceTitle: Performing Arts | Penn Admissions

facts.title: The Daily Pennsylvanian
facts.summary: The Daily Pennsylvanian is Penn's independent student media organization, publishing news, sports, and entertainment coverage of Penn and the Philadelphia area about 116 mornings a year.
facts.hook: gives student journalists a newsroom covering Penn and the Philadelphia metro area
facts.quote: The Daily Pennsylvanian (DP)—recognized as one of the top college newspapers in the country—is Penn’s independent student media organization. About 116 mornings each school year, Penn students, faculty and staff turn to the DP for news, sports, and entertainment coverage about the Philadelphia metro area and Penn.
facts.sourceTitle: Media and Communications | Penn Admissions
facts.commonnessReason: A standard student newspaper featured on admissions pages; most schools have an equivalent.

facts.title: Hayden Scholars
facts.summary: Hayden Scholars builds a community of undergraduate geoscience researchers through independent research experiences affiliated with Penn's Department of Earth and Environmental Science.
facts.hook: builds a community of undergraduate geoscience researchers through independent research experiences
facts.quote: The Hayden Scholars program aims to build a community of undergraduate researchers in the geosciences at Penn through extra-curricular, independent research experiences affiliated with the Department of Earth and Environmental Science.
facts.sourceTitle: Undergraduate Research | Earth and Environmental Sciences

facts.title: Kleinman Center for Energy Policy Student Grants
facts.summary: The Kleinman Center for Energy Policy has funded more than 200 Penn student grants, from research to conferences, offered four times a year to individual students and student groups.
facts.hook: funds student research and conference grants four times a year, open to individuals and student groups
facts.quote: From research to conferences, the Kleinman Center has funded more than 200 Penn student grants. Grants are offered four times per year in the spring, summer, fall, and winter, and are open to individual students as well as student groups.
facts.sourceTitle: Student Grants - Kleinman Center for Energy Policy

facts.title: Kleinman Center Undergraduate Climate & Energy Policy Seminar
facts.summary: The Kleinman Center's selective seminar for committed undergraduates meets four to six times a semester to hear energy researchers discuss the findings and policy implications of their work.
facts.hook: selects undergraduate fellows to hear energy researchers discuss the policy implications of their work
facts.quote: This program is designed as a competitive and selective appointment for committed undergraduates. Admitted students are expected to attend 4-6 seminars over the course of the semester at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy. These sessions provide students with the opportunity to meet and hear from energy researchers as they discuss the findings and policy implications of their recent research.
facts.sourceTitle: Undergraduate Seminar - Kleinman Center for Energy Policy

facts.title: Penn Abroad
facts.summary: Penn Abroad sends over 2,500 students a year to more than 50 countries for semester study abroad, summer internships, service learning, and short-term programs.
facts.hook: sends students to more than 50 countries for study abroad, internships, and service learning
facts.quote: Penn Abroad serves as the hub for student global opportunities at Penn. Each year the University sends over 2,500 Penn students to more than 50 countries around the world on semester study abroad, summer internships, service learning, and short-term programs.
facts.sourceTitle: Off-campus Learning | University of Pennsylvania
facts.commonnessReason: Study abroad offices exist at nearly every university and are often cited generically.

facts.title: Penn Adventure outdoor trips (Campus Recreation)
facts.summary: Campus Recreation's outdoor adventure trips range from scenic day trips to multi-day expeditions in the Greater Philadelphia area and beyond.
facts.hook: takes students on day trips and multi-day outdoor expeditions near Philadelphia and beyond
facts.quote: Whether you're looking for a scenic day trip or a multi-day expedition, our outdoor adventure trips program has you covered. Penn Adventure trips can take you to local destinations in the Greater Philadelphia area or outside of the state
facts.sourceTitle: Outdoor Trips - Penn Campus Recreation
facts.commonnessReason: A campus-recreation outdoor trips program like those at many universities.

facts.title: Penn Green Fund
facts.summary: Penn's Green Fund accepts ideas from students, faculty, staff, and postdocs for improving the University's environmental performance and cutting campus emissions, with awards up to $30,000.
facts.hook: funds student-proposed campus sustainability projects with awards of up to $30,000
facts.quote: Penn’s Green Fund welcomes ideas from students, faculty, staff, and postdocs about ways to improve the University’s environmental performance and reduce campus emissions. ... There is no minimum award for a Green Fund application and the maximum award is $30,000.
facts.sourceTitle: Green Fund | Penn Sustainability

facts.title: Penn IUR Undergraduate Urban Research Colloquium (UURC)
facts.summary: The Penn Institute for Urban Research's colloquium pairs faculty doing urban-focused research with undergraduates in a semester-long, credit-bearing research seminar.
facts.hook: pairs undergraduates with faculty doing urban research in a credit-bearing seminar
facts.quote: This innovative research program pairs faculty conducting urban-focused scholarship with undergraduates that have an interest in developing research skills in a semester-long, credit-bearing seminar.
facts.sourceTitle: Student Programs | Penn IUR

facts.title: Penn Model Organization of American States (Penn Model OAS)
facts.summary: Penn Model OAS pairs Penn undergraduates with Philadelphia-area public high school students who prepare as diplomats for an annual Model OAS simulation in Washington, D.C., including public speaking.
facts.hook: has Penn students help Philadelphia-area high schoolers prepare as diplomats for an annual Model OAS simulation
facts.quote: Students come from public high schools across in Philadelphia and the Norristown area to work with Penn college students in preparing to serve as “diplomats” in the annual Model OAS simulation in Washington, D.C. in late fall. ... They also engage in public speaking, and interact with policy experts, public officials, and leading scholars in the field.
facts.sourceTitle: Welcome to Penn Model OAS | Center for Latin American and Latinx Studies

facts.title: Penn Undergraduate Research Mentoring Program (PURM)
facts.summary: PURM lets first- and second-year Penn students spend a summer doing research under a standing Penn faculty member, with no prior research experience required.
facts.hook: gives first- and second-year students a summer of faculty-mentored research with no experience required
facts.quote: PURM provides Penn students completing their first or second undergraduate year the opportunity to spend a summer conducting cutting-edge research under the guidance of a standing Penn faculty member. No prior experience is required.
facts.sourceTitle: Funding Opportunities | Penn CURF
facts.commonnessReason: A well-publicized Penn research program that some applicants mention.

facts.title: PennGreen Pre-Orientation Program
facts.summary: PennGreen is a pre-orientation program for incoming students that explores local green spaces, sustainable food networks, and sustainability pathways, with an overnight camping trip as a highlight.
facts.hook: introduces incoming students to local green spaces and sustainability pathways, with an overnight camping trip
facts.quote: PennGreen is a Pre-Orientation Program for incoming students sponsored by Penn Sustainability and the Undergraduate Assembly. ... discovering local green spaces, exploring sustainable food networks, learning about academic and extracurricular pathways in sustainability ... A highlight of the program is an overnight camping trip.
facts.sourceTitle: PennGreen | Penn Sustainability

facts.title: Spanish for Healthcare Professionals & Cultural Immersion in Oaxaca (NURS 2980)
facts.summary: Penn Nursing's six-week field course in Oaxaca, Mexico, has rising juniors, seniors, and graduate students practice Spanish in health care settings with local partners such as Clinica Del Pueblo.
facts.hook: has students practice Spanish in Oaxaca health care settings with local community partners
facts.quote: Rising juniors, seniors, and graduate students ... a six-week immersive field experience in the vibrant cultural landscape of Oaxaca, Mexico. ... Master your Spanish Skills in Healthcare settings by applying your skills in practical, real-world settings. ... Connect with the Community through meaningful engagement with our local partners, Instituto Cultural Oaxaca, Fundacion En Via and Clinica Del Pueblo.
facts.sourceTitle: Spanish for Healthcare Professionals & Cultural Immersion in Oaxaca • Global Health • Penn Nursing

facts.title: Student Eco-Reps
facts.summary: Each year 10 to 20 sophomores, juniors, and seniors are selected as paid Eco-Reps who work with Penn's Sustainability Office, developing small-scale pilots and then broader implementation.
facts.hook: pays students to develop and pilot sustainability projects with Penn's Sustainability Office
facts.quote: Students work as paid employees of Penn’s Sustainability Office ... Each year, a cohort of 10-20 Penn sophomores, juniors, and seniors are selected to participate in the Eco-Reps program. ... developing small-scale pilots, and then focusing on broader implementation.
facts.sourceTitle: Student Eco-Reps | Penn Sustainability

facts.title: The Marian Anderson Performance Program (MUSC 0100)
facts.summary: This auditioned Music Department program, open to music majors and minors, provides performance instruction in classical, jazz, and world music traditions.
facts.hook: offers auditioned performance instruction in jazz, classical, and world music for music majors and minors
facts.quote: This program is open to music majors and minors only. ... The Department of Music supports a wide variety of performance traditions and encourages qualified students to apply for instruction in classical, jazz, and world music traditions.
facts.sourceTitle: The Marian Anderson Performance Program | Department of Music

facts.title: The Roy and Diana Vagelos Integrated Program in Energy Research (VIPER)
facts.nameOnPage: The Roy and Diana Vagelos Integrated Program in Energy Research
facts.summary: VIPER is a coordinated dual-degree program in energy research in which students earn a BA from the College of Arts and Sciences and a BS in Engineering from Penn Engineering.
facts.hook: combines a College BA with an engineering BS for students focused on energy research
facts.quote: The Roy and Diana Vagelos Integrated Program in Energy Research ... Students earn a BA from the College of Arts and Sciences and a BS in Engineering from the School of Engineering and Applied Science.
facts.sourceTitle: Interdisciplinary | University of Pennsylvania
facts.commonnessReason: A known specialized program with its own application; energy-focused applicants often mention it.

facts.title: Convocation at Franklin Field
facts.summary: Convocation at Franklin Field is Penn's traditional welcome ceremony for the incoming class and new transfer students, with remarks and musical performances.
facts.hook: welcomes each new class at Franklin Field with remarks and musical performances
facts.quote: hosted the Convocation Ceremony ... at Franklin Field. This ceremony is Penn's traditional welcome to the Class of ... and new transfer students as they join the Penn community, with remarks and musical performances.
facts.sourceTitle: University of Pennsylvania
facts.commonnessReason: Most universities hold a convocation; useful mainly for the swap test.

facts.title: Hey Day
facts.summary: Hey Day, which marks juniors becoming seniors, is today Penn's most notable student tradition and incorporates elements of many past and present traditions.
facts.hook: marks the passage of juniors to seniors in Penn's most notable annual tradition
facts.quote: Today the most notable is the annual Hey Day event which incorporates elements of many other traditions past and present. ... Hey Day as an event to mark the passing of juniors to seniors of the College has its origins in a ceremony that was part of the senior’s Class Day in 1889.
facts.sourceTitle: Penn Student Traditions: Hey Day
facts.commonnessReason: Penn's best-known student tradition, widely cited by applicants.

facts.title: Penn Relays
facts.summary: First held in 1895, the Penn Relays Carnival is the country's longest-running track and field meet, attracting more than 100,000 spectators and 15,000 entries each year.
facts.hook: brings more than 100,000 spectators to campus each year for the longest-running US track meet
facts.quote: First held on April 21, 1895, the Penn Relays Carnival is the longest running track & field meet in the country ... more than 100,000 spectators and more than 15,000 entries each year.
facts.sourceTitle: Athletics & Recreation | University of Pennsylvania
facts.commonnessReason: A famous Penn tradition that many applicants mention.
